clue.text: A land once curtailed? No, a huge region

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter of the old country's name goes

parts.note: Siam is a land once, the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a shrunken former country, answered with a rebuttal pointing to a vast area.
explanation.walkthrough: Thailand's former name loses its final letter under 'curtailed'. The question followed by 'No' makes the clue seem to contradict itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent on Earth, an enormous region of land.

clue.text: At last restricting new spies in terms of resources?

indicators.note: restricting means holding something in, so the phrase for at last encloses the other pieces

parts.note: at last means finally
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Someone finally limiting fresh intelligence agents because money is short.
explanation.definitionFit: Financially means with regard to money and funds, which are a body's resources.

clue.text: Grip tightly boy caught in church

indicators.note: in places the boy's name within the letters for caught and church set side by side

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

explanation.surface: Someone holding tight to a lad who has been nabbed inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To clench is to close or grasp firmly, as with a fist or the teeth.

clue.text: Suppress lecturer in party operating around county

indicators.note: around tells us the party-plus-operating letters wrap about the county's name
in puts the lecturer's letter inside the word for party

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party, as in a political camp
on means operating or working, as a machine is on
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A political faction, with an academic inside, active in some county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland. 'around' wraps the party-with-lecturer and operating pieces about the county, splitting them.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamp down on something is to act firmly to stop or restrict it.

clue.text: Victor missed in hectic evening — a dynamo?

indicators.note: hectic suggests frantic disorder, so the remaining letters are scrambled
missed means left out, so the letter for Victor is dropped from the word

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A frantic night out without Victor, who was the life and soul of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking V out of EVENING leaves EENING, which 'hectic' rearranges. 'a dynamo?' reads like a lively person, but here it is a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator, a machine that produces power, much like a motor or power unit.

clue.text: Bill interrupts frantic search for game

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle, so the bill's letters go inside
frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters of search are rearranged

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advert, AD for short

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives in the middle of a desperate hunt for some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges the six letters into CHARES, which 'interrupts' then opens after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party guessing game in which words are mimed.

clue.text: Take hold of snack

definitions.meaning: to grip with the teeth or grab, as a fish takes the hook
a mouthful or light morsel of food

explanation.surface: Grab a quick bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip with the teeth is to take hold; a quick morsel of food is also a small meal of this kind.

clue.text: Foundation above lake in European city

indicators.note: above in a down entry means coming first, on top of the next piece

parts.note: a base is a foundation

explanation.surface: A building's footing sits over a lake in a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'above' places BASE before L.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine.

clue.text: Brown raising a glass?

definitions.meaning: to brown bread under a grill
lifting drinks in honour of someone

explanation.surface: A person called Brown lifting a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname, perhaps a politician, but it is the verb for grilling bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To brown bread is to grill it; a salute with drinks in someone's honour is the same word.

clue.text: Waste second tablet

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: Throwing away a further dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill liquid is to let it run out and be lost, so wasted.

clue.text: A fellow possibly aghast in new country

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A man perhaps horrified on arrival in an unfamiliar land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the eight letters into GHANISTA. 'fellow' looks like a person in the surface but just gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanistan is a landlocked nation in Central Asia.

clue.text: Scare infecting national army

indicators.note: infecting means getting inside, so the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fright spreading through a country's military.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a sudden fright or fear, so a scare.

clue.text: Versatile sportsman leapt the net amazingly

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishing, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An all-round athlete astonishingly jumps over the tennis net.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentathlete competes in five different events, so must be a multi-skilled athlete.

clue.text: Complaint after bloody pump malfunctions?

parts.note: the bloody pump is the organ that circulates blood; its failure brings on a serious medical complaint

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling after a wretched machine pump breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' reads as a British mild swear word, but it literally means full of blood; 'Complaint' is an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronary is a medical complaint that follows the failure of the organ pumping blood.

clue.text: Former custom producing court surrender

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
a tradition is a custom

explanation.surface: An old practice leads a court to hand something over.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is a legal handover of an accused person by one state to another, ordered by a court.

clue.text: Book place in NW England

definitions.meaning: an abbreviation for Ecclesiastes, a book of the Old Testament
a town near Manchester, famous for its currant cakes

explanation.surface: Reserve a spot in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb, to reserve, but it is a book of the Bible in short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastes, a biblical book, shortens to this; it is also a town in Greater Manchester.

clue.text: Turned rickety car in front of drive

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled
front of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A ramshackle car parked at the front of someone's driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges CAR IN into RANCI, and 'front of' adds D from 'drive'. 'Turned' is the definition, as milk turns sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone off, smelling sour or stale.

clue.text: Mavis sadly concealing love for sci-fi writer

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the rearranged name holds the extra letter
sadly signals the letters of the name are put in a sorry state, rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Poor Mavis is secretly in love with a science-fiction author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MAVIS into ASIMV, and 'concealing' places O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific American science-fiction novelist, author of I, Robot.

clue.text: Scan item for review regarding meaning of terms

indicators.note: for review suggests going over again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Examine an article to check what its words mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic describes anything relating to the meaning of words and language.

clue.text: A graduate beginning to study in time a lot of files?

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A graduate starting to research some records within a given period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' supplies S, and 'in' places the four letters after the third letter of the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a large organised store of computer records.

clue.text: Table with dates, cold drink and odd bit of refreshment

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the little word is rearranged
bit of picks just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cool beer and a strange snack taken with dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges AND into NDA, then 'bit of' adds R from 'refreshment'. 'dates' look like fruit to eat, but they are days.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a chart listing the days and months of the year.

clue.text: Servicemen in road close to house form attack

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
the RAF, Royal Air Force, are British servicemen

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Airmen in a street near a house ready to launch an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's air force. 'close to' takes E from 'house'; 'form' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Ancient old boy turning up in wine shop

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means written from bottom to top, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: aged means ancient or very old
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An elderly former pupil appears in a wine merchant's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AGED + OB as one run, making BODEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling wine.

clue.text: A duty Andy and I discharged pocketing nothing constantly

indicators.note: pocketing means putting into a pocket, so the jumbled letters enclose another
discharged suggests released and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, written O

explanation.surface: Andy and I, relieved of a task, kept nothing for ourselves, all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' rearranges A DUTY ANDY I, and 'pocketing' puts O inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every single day without end is done continually.

clue.text: Quick-moving soldier in valley without leader

indicators.note: in places the soldier's letters within what is left of the valley
without leader means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a dale is a valley
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier moving swiftly through a valley after losing his commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' leaves ALE, which 'in' opens to take the American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble, able to move quickly and easily.

clue.text: At home with pet mongrel? That's awkward

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Indoors with a crossbreed dog, which proves troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' looks like a description of the dog, but it rearranges PET to EPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, so ungainly.

clue.text: Slated item includes origin of this right

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the roofing word encloses a letter

parts.note: a tile, as slates on a roof are tiles

indicators.note: origin of picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A criticised article contains the beginning of this right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slated' looks like criticised, but here it means roofed with slates. T, first of 'this', goes inside TILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a legal claim or entitlement to property.

clue.text: Peer mostly ahead

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is usually in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look, but it is a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Filming device in arcade movie deployed

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A camera is set up in an amusement arcade to shoot a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A video camera is a device for recording moving pictures.

clue.text: Macho Irishman suppressing a source of harmony?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the answer is contained within the words

explanation.surface: A tough Irishman holding down something that brings peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmony' suggests peaceful agreement, but it is singing in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir sings in parts, producing musical harmony.

clue.text: Transported a little money, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A few coins dispatched somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something is to convey it elsewhere, so it has been carried away.

clue.text: Us city having modern refuge from deluge?

parts.note: new means modern
Noah's ark was the refuge from the Flood

explanation.surface: An American town with a brand-new shelter from floods.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark is a large city in New Jersey, in the United States.
